svg.title: Where a Checkpoint Lives and How a Restore Finds It
svg.desc: A capture writes the checkpoint to its node's disk, registers the node as the checkpoint's first source, and copies it in the background to an rwx volume that is promoted to a read-only rox volume. A restore takes the first copy it finds: its own disk, a shared filesystem when one is configured, the rox volume, then the agents that hold it, over HTTP, those it has the fewest fetches in flight from first. Every node that fetches becomes a source.
svg.text: Where a Checkpoint Lives and How a Restore Finds It
Numbers 1-4 are the order a restore tries. Dashed: only when configured.
captures, then copies in the background
HTTP, large files spread across them
becomes a source once it has a copy
takes the first copy it finds
a copy already here is used as is
A copy on the restoring node's own disk is used as is. 2 Then a shared filesystem, when the cluster has one. 3 Then a copy from the checkpoint's rox volume.
Then the agents the catalog lists as sources, those this agent has the fewest fetches in flight from first; when several hold the checkpoint, its large files are fetched from all of them at
once. A node that fetched registers itself as a source.
Not in this order: an object-store bucket shared between clusters (L4), which opt-in replication fills and pulls from in the background.
